articles.title: Táxis sem motorista da Tesla são investigados nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Órgão federal de segurança viária abriu investigação para verificar se a Tesla certificou corretamente o Cybercab, que não tem volante, pedais de freio ou acelerador.
articles.summary: Órgão federal de segurança viária abriu investigação para verificar se a Tesla certificou corretamente o Cybercab, que não tem volante, pedais de freio ou acelerador.
articles.body:
A Administração Nacional de Segurança no Trânsito dos Estados Unidos (NHTSA) abriu nesta sexta-feira (4) uma investigação para verificar se a Tesla certificou corretamente seu robotáxi autônomo Cybercab.

A perícia vai analisar o processo e os dados técnicos usados pela montadora para demonstrar que até 1.000 Cybercabs atendiam aos padrões federais de segurança para veículos.

Na quinta-feira (3), a Tesla começou a colocar em operação comercial um pequeno número de Cybercabs de dois lugares em Austin, no Texas. A empresa afirmou que pretende ampliar gradualmente o serviço para mais veículos e outras localidades.

Segundo a NHTSA, o Cybercab não possui controles manuais convencionais, como volante, pedal de freio, pedal do acelerador e espelhos retrovisores.

As montadoras precisam declarar que seus veículos cumprem os padrões federais de segurança. Quando há indícios de que um veículo certificado não atende a essas exigências, a NHTSA abre uma investigação, afirmou a agência.

A investigação vai analisar a base usada pela Tesla para certificar o Cybercab e outros pontos relacionados, incluindo até que ponto a empresa considerou que determinadas exigências de segurança não se aplicavam ao veículo.

“A NHTSA apoia totalmente o desenvolvimento e a implantação seguros de veículos automatizados. Mas, como órgão regulador federal, precisamos garantir que todas as nossas leis sejam cumpridas”, disse Jonathan Morrison, administrador da NHTSA.

A Tesla não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

Tesla Cybercab — Foto: Divulgação / Tesla

Regras atuais ainda exigem controles humanos

Em junho, a NHTSA propôs acabar com uma exigência do governo que determina a presença de pedais de freio manuais em veículos autônomos. A mudança facilitaria a colocação desses veículos nas ruas dos Estados Unidos.

A agência também propôs outras alterações nos padrões federais de segurança para permitir que veículos autônomos deixem de ter alguns equipamentos destinados a motoristas humanos.

Até que essas mudanças sejam concluídas, porém, as regras atuais continuam valendo, afirmou a NHTSA.

Pelas regras em vigor, veículos totalmente autônomos não precisam de aprovação da NHTSA se tiverem os controles humanos exigidos, como volante, pedais de freio ou espelhos.

A NHTSA pode autorizar até 2.500 veículos por fabricante a circular anualmente nas ruas dos Estados Unidos sem os controles humanos exigidos.

Em julho, a agência aprovou um pedido da Zoox , empresa da Amazon, para colocar de forma limitada em operação comercial seus novos robotáxis sem volante. Foi a primeira autorização desse tipo para o setor de transporte autônomo.

Zoox, táxi sem volantes e pedais da Amazon, recebe autorização para operar nos EUA — Foto: Divulgação / Zoox

Segundo a NHTSA, a Tesla não havia apresentado um pedido de autorização semelhante.

Até a manhã desta sexta-feira, havia 420 veículos autônomos da Tesla registrados no Texas, segundo dados do estado. Desse total, 45 eram Cybercabs.

articles.title: Gato-do-mato-pequeno é flagrado em Rio Claro | G1
articles.standfirst: Registro foi feito em uma área de Mata Atlântica por onde passa a Trilha Volta das Águas.
articles.summary: Registro foi feito em uma área de Mata Atlântica por onde passa a Trilha Volta das Águas.
articles.body:
Gato-do-mato-pequeno é flagrado próximo ao Centro de Lídice, em Rio Claro — Foto: Ronald César Tavares

Um gato-do-mato-pequeno foi flagrado na sexta-feira (4) em uma área próxima ao centro de Lídice, distrito de Rio Claro (RJ). O registro foi feito pelo fotógrafo e observador de aves Ronald César Tavares, enquanto ele fotografava pássaros na região.

Segundo o fotógrafo, o animal estava próximo ao trecho da linha férrea que corta o distrito, em uma área de Mata Atlântica. Ele já teve outras oportunidades de encontrar a espécie na região e também registrou animais por meio de câmeras de trilha.

Entre os animais já identificados por ele na região estão veados, porcos-do-mato, pacas e cotias. Em dezembro do ano passado, ele também conseguiu registrar uma jaguatirica.

O local onde o gato-do-mato foi fotografado fica próximo à linha férrea e integra um trecho da Trilha Volta das Águas de Rio Claro. Com mais de 310 quilômetros de extensão, a trilha é considerada a maior trilha de longo curso do Brasil localizada integralmente dentro de um único município.

A Trilha Volta das Águas é multimodal e podendo ser percorrida a pé, a cavalo, de bicicleta e por meio de trechos de canoagem.

De acordo com a Prefeitura de Rio Claro, a presença e os registros de animais silvestres na região reforçam a importância da preservação dos remanescentes de Mata Atlântica no município.

articles.title: People drive miles for this California beach town's 'miracle' water. I went to see what keeps them coming back.
articles.summary: Carlsbad's wellness culture didn't start with luxury spas or sound baths. It started with a mineral well in the 1880s.
articles.body:
It's an early Thursday afternoon in Carlsbad, California, and several short lines stretch like tentacles from a kiosk in the middle of town .

In line, visitors and locals juggle an array of glass containers — some piled onto carts — waiting for their turn at one of the available spigots. Nearby, a woman shouts in the general direction of my group: "This is the best water in the world!" Is she a walking covert Carlsbad ad placement? Surprisingly, no. Turns out, she makes this pilgrimage once a week. The water, she says, has changed her life.

Since the 1880s, people have been coming to Carlsbad for mineral water credited with treating all manner of ailments. Standing in line with my own bottle, I wondered whether the miracle water was just a quirky local thing or the beginning of Carlsbad's surprisingly deep-rooted wellness culture.

So, what ' s the deal with Carlsbad ' s ' miracle ' water?

The structure that dispenses the water isn't much to look at — a tiny Bavarian-style building that seems to have lost its way to Oktoberfest. But even so, people come for what's said to emerge from a 1,700-foot-deep aquifer fed by water that drains from the Cleveland National Forest, allegedly untouched by anything except time and pressure.

The business behind the wells says the water's pH hovers around 8.7 — solidly alkaline — and those who journey for a taste believe the water detoxifies, hydrates, oxygenates, alkalizes and enhances the body's immune system. Mayo Clinic , on the other hand, says that for most people, alkaline water is no better than plain water, and more research is needed to support its purported health benefits.

But whether the water is a miracle worker or just tastes a little better than tap is almost irrelevant now. Its devotees believe it to be true, and a mini-wellness industry has sprung up around it.

From mineral well to wellness destination

The man behind the well was John Frazier, a merchant seaman and farmer. According to local accounts, Frazier drilled a well in 1882 while searching for regular drinking water and hit something else entirely. As the story goes, he had suffered from stomach ailments and believed he felt better after drinking the water. Historical accounts say he sent samples to independent labs, which found that the mineral composition was similar to that of the famous healing waters of Karlovy Vary in the Czech Republic.

The settlement, informally known as Frazier's Station, soon took the name Carlsbad — an anglicized version of Karlsbad, the German name for Karlovy Vary — after tests reportedly found similarities between the two places' mineral waters.

By the late 1880s, the Carlsbad Hotel had opened near the well, drawing visitors from around the country. It became the centerpiece of a town that had established itself as a health and wellness destination, with guests coming to drink and bathe in its "miracle" alkaline waters. The water was also bottled and sold nationally, extending Carlsbad's reputation well beyond those who came in person.

The original Carlsbad Hotel burned to the ground in 1896. More than three decades later, a new property, the California-Carlsbad Mineral Springs Hotel, opened across the street from the springs. But the well fell into disrepair during the Depression and remained out of service for decades.

Ludvik and Veronica Grigoras began restoring and redrilling the wells in 1993. Ludvik, who was born in Karlovy Vary, was passionate about the well's history and building a relationship between the sister cities. By 1996, his vision was realized when the well reopened and the alkaline mineral water was available to the public yet again.

Today, Carlsbad is home to some of the best resort spas in the country, rebooted for an audience that says "adaptogen" instead of "tonic."

The sprawling Omni La Costa Resort & Spa is a lush 400-acre, Spanish Mission-style enclave that feels like its own mini-wellness city. Hotel Solea shares a hilltop campus with the Westin, including its spa. (If you're traveling with kids, Solea offers private LEGOLAND access, which you can use as leverage for a quiet moment in your room.)

But my absolute favorite Carlsbad retreat is Beach Terrace , one of the rare stays in town that butts up directly against the roaring waves of the Pacific. The rooms are beyond spacious, and there were a few nights when I left the sliding glass doors open — the waves served as the best white-noise machine on the market. There's no spa on the premises, but you can arrange an in-room massage after a day of shopping in nearby downtown Carlsbad (retail therapy counts as wellness).

Happy Blue Marble runs sound baths where you lie on a mat under low light while crystal bowls and chimes wash over you — the kind of thing that seems a bit woo-woo until the moment you're horizontal.

Paddleboard the calm waters of Agua Hedionda Lagoon and pair it with an afternoon at Handled Pottery Studio , where a large garage door stays open to the street, letting the cool Carlsbad air drift through while you throw a piece. For a meal that keeps you moving, the Carlsbad Food Tour walks you through the downtown Carlsbad restaurant scene with actual context instead of just a list of Yelp links.

Even Carlsbad's biggest attractions sneak in some wellness. The Flower Fields at Carlsbad Ranch bloom across 55 acres of ranunculus every spring, and walking the rows is essentially a moving meditation with better photo ops.

Leo Carrillo Ranch Historic Park offers the same effect in a different way, with 27 acres of shaded trails, wandering peacocks and rustic buildings. It's the kind of place that lowers your heart rate without you even noticing.

San Diego International Airport (SAN) is the main gateway to the area, though limited commercial flights also serve Carlsbad's smaller McClellan-Palomar Airport (CLD). Carlsbad is roughly 35 to 45 minutes north of SAN without heavy traffic, though I-5 rush hour can stretch that significantly, so build in a buffer if you're catching a flight.

Most visitors rent a car. The big resorts sit inland, meaning you'll drive to the beach or wait for a rideshare option to come along.

Carlsbad stays mild year-round, with its warmest and driest weather generally arriving from July through October. If the Flower Fields are the draw, come in spring; the attraction typically operates from March into May.

The well has self-serve dispensers that run 24 hours a day and charge $1.40 per gallon. It only takes cash, so you'll have to bring dollar bills and some loose change to get your goods. Bring an empty cooler if you're planning to leave with more water than you arrived with — most people do.

images.caption: Before Carlsbad became a wellness destination, visitors were coming for the well. (Art Wager via Getty Images)
Is the water a gimmick or the real deal? Depends who you ask. (Jackie Gutierrez-Jones)
Beyond its spas and wellness scene, Carlsbad is also famous for its massive flower field. (Kelly Chen via Getty Images)

articles.title: ‘Developed countries must take lead': India calls for climate finance after Nepal flood
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday said developed countries must take the lead in reducing emissions and support developing nations.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday said developed countries must take the lead in reducing emissions and support developing nations through finance and technology transfer, reiterating India's position that climate action must be guided by the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.The remarks by MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal came in the aftermath of the devastating flash floods in Nepal and amid questions over remarks concerning climate-related compensation from major economies, including India, China and the United States.‘Climate change is a common challenge’Addressing the issue at a weekly media briefing, Jaiswal said India had consistently maintained that climate change was a shared challenge.“I understand that a clarification has also been issued by the Nepalese side. Having said that, let me say that India has consistently maintained that climate change is a common challenge, and action in this regard must be based on the principle of common differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities,” he said.Jaiswal said countries historically responsible for emissions should take the lead in tackling the challenge and supporting developing nations.“Developed countries who historically are responsible for the emissions and have contributed overwhelmingly to the civil crisis, must take lead in reducing emissions and supporting developing countries by way of finance and technology transfer to meet this challenge,” the MEA spokesperson added.India reiterates support for NepalJaiswal also said India had extended solidarity and support to Nepal following the tragedy and would continue to assist the country in its reconstruction and recovery efforts.“In the wake of this tragedy, we have extended our solidarity and support to the government and people of Nepal. As a close friend and partner, India responded promptly, and we will continue to support the reconstruction and recovery efforts in the country,” he said.Referring to Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah's appreciation of India's assistance, Jaiswal said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had spoken to his Nepalese counterpart after the disaster and conveyed India's support.“We have seen that the Prime Minister of Nepal has thanked us for our support... our prime minister spoke to the Prime Minister of Nepal and conveyed that India stands shoulder to shoulder and extends all its support to Nepal in this time of crisis, and it will offer whatever help is required,” he said.Nepal clarifies compensation remarksMeanwhile, Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal clarified on Thursday that neither he nor the Nepalese government had sought climate-related compensation from India, China or the United States.“Neither I nor anyone in the ministry of foreign affairs or the government of Nepal has claimed or asked for compensation from India or any other country, including China or the United States,” Khanal told news agency ANI.Also read: Nepal minister clarifies 'compensation from world' remark after flash floodsHe said Nepal's appeal was for the global community to recognise climate change and its impact on the country.“Our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in Nepal,” he added.Khanal also said India, China and Nepal shared environmental ecosystems and should work together to prepare for the impact of climate change in the Himalayas.He stressed the need to look beyond one-time disaster assistance and consider the longer-term effects of rising temperatures and climate change on communities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Pupil stabs teacher in head with kitchen knife after asking her to check homework; sentenced for 4 years
articles.summary: UK News: A 16-year-old boy receives a four-and-a-half year youth detention sentence after a brutal stabbing of a teacher with a kitchen knife during a homework check at Milford Haven Comprehensive School. The incident has raised significant concerns about school safety and violence against teachers.
articles.body: A 16-year-old boy has been sentenced to four-and-a-half years in youth detention after stabbing a teacher in the head with a kitchen knife when he asked her to check his homework, BBC reported.The teenager attacked Vicki Williams inside an empty classroom at Milford Haven Comprehensive School in Pembrokeshire on February 5. He had approached her after the school day and asked whether his work was correct.Williams told the court during the trial that the attack happened without warning. After entering the classroom, the boy closed the door and began looking through his bag before pulling out a large kitchen knife and lunging at her.She suffered injuries to her head, back and hands. Williams managed to grab the knife and push the teenager away with her legs before screaming for help.She later told the court that she feared she was going to die and was left struggling with the psychological impact of the attack. She is due to begin treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder and said she was unsure whether she would be able to return to teaching.The teenager, who cannot be named because of his age and a court order, was acquitted of attempted murder following a trial in July. He was convicted of wounding with intent and had already pleaded guilty to possessing a bladed article on school premises.The court heard that he told the jury he had taken the knife to school as part of a game with friends involving bringing random household objects to school to see what they could get away with. He described the stabbing as an accident.Judge Paul Thomas said there had been a “significant degree of planning” behind the attack. He also said it was “pure luck” that Williams did not suffer much more serious or fatal injuries.The judge said the teenager had taken the knife to school because he intended to seriously hurt Williams, although he said the boy had never explained why he attacked her.After the stabbing, CCTV showed the teenager leaving the school. He was later found at his grandmother’s home after telling her that “something went” in his head.The court heard Williams returned to the school during the summer with a colleague and realised how closely she had been pinned against the wall behind her desk during the attack.Her colleagues were also affected by the incident. One teacher who went to help described hearing Williams's screams as “gut-wrenching”.The defence told the court that the teenager had no previous convictions and had been well behaved before the attack. His lawyer Matthew Roberts said he had made good progress while in youth detention.The teenager is expected to be released after serving half of his sentence, although the court heard that could change if the rules governing early release are amended.The judge also pointed to the April 2024 attack at Ysgol Dyffryn Aman, where two teachers and a pupil were stabbed, stressing the need to protect school staff from violence.The Crown Prosecution Service described the incident as a shocking act of violence against a teacher who was carrying out her job.Milford Haven Comprehensive School was placed under lockdown following the attack. The local council said only a small number of pupils were on the premises at the time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jaishankar says India in touch with Russia, Ukraine to help end war
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday said India has been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and is exploring whet.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday said India has been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and is exploring whether ideas and suggestions can be developed to contribute to the mitigation and, ideally, the cessation of the conflict.Jaishankar made the remarks in Warsaw after holding talks with Poland's deputy Prime Minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, a day after he met the top Ukrainian leadership in Kyiv.‘Endless war must give way to an end to war’Addressing a joint press meet with Sikorski, Jaishankar said the two leaders discussed major global and regional issues, including the war in Ukraine, which is now in its fifth year.“The deputy Prime Minister and I also understandably discussed some major global and regional issues, notable among them is the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year... I myself have just come here from Kyiv,” he said.Replying to a question, Jaishankar said India remained in touch with both sides.“What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,” he added.Jaishankar reiterated India's position that the conflict must end through dialogue and diplomacy.“India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war. These are wars without winners. Every additional day means more death, more destruction, more loss to the parties themselves, and more cost to the rest of the world,” he said.“Our efforts must therefore focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. We must each do what we can in whichever way we believe could be most effective and support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it,” he added.Jaishankar rejects trade link to ending warResponding to a question on India's purchases of Russian oil, Jaishankar said the solution to the conflict lay in negotiations rather than trade.“This war is not going to end... not because somebody chose to buy or not buy oil or alumina or fertilisers or metals and minerals. It will end when there is diplomacy, when there is dialogue and when there is negotiation. So, I think let's diagnose the problem right,” he said.A day earlier in Kyiv, Jaishankar had met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and foreign minister Andrii Sybiha and said India was ready to extend “any help in any manner” to help end the war.Following the meeting, Zelenskyy said he was “grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war”.India-Poland talks cover trade, technology and securityJaishankar and Sikorski also discussed complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security.The two ministers reviewed the progress of the India-Poland Joint Action Plan 2024-28, covering areas including trade and investment, space, digital technology, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, defence, education, shipping, mining and energy.Jaishankar also called on Polish President Karol Nawrocki and discussed the trajectory of the India-Poland Strategic Partnership, as well as the Ukraine conflict and developments in West Asia.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Influencers are everywhere at the U.S. Open. Even tennis stars say it's gone too far.
articles.summary: Tennis players know that the presence of influencers at their matches is good for the popularity of the sport — but at what cost?
articles.body:
It's struck Coachella , fashion week and even summers in Nantucket . Now, influencer fatigue has come for the U.S. Open.

For two weeks every year, the notoriously ritzy tennis tournament attracts fans, celebrities and bougie vibe enthusiasts, who navigate long lines to the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Queens, N.Y., to watch matches and be seen doing so.

It's got all the trappings of content creator heaven : Viral food and drinks to taste test, limited-edition merchandise to purchase, stars to rub elbows with, fashion trends to spot and iconic imagery that instantly makes social media posts recognizable. As some have pointed out, it's inherently a bit performative .

"Tennis has always married sport with spectacle, and fashion, celebrity and luxury are genuinely part of the Open's DNA," Soneca Guadara, a longtime U.S. Open attendee and style consultant, told Yahoo. " From a marketing standpoint, it makes perfect sense that creators want to be there."

So why is the presence of influencers a problem at all? It's more than just disdain for the privileged and wealthy, which influencers often face at other luxury events. This year, it's what some view as bad behavior during matches that's drawing ire.

Traditionally, it's proper etiquette at tennis matches to be quiet and respectful during play — more so than at other sporting events, like basketball or football games — and that decorum is typically enforced by the chair umpire.

But an Instagram post that went viral this week shows a woman posing for photos with a selfie light on during Naomi Osaka's first-round match against Anastasia Zakharova. Later in the video, a gaggle of attendees is seen filming content in a suite. Another video from a different angle caught the same group, with a fan seated below them appearing disgruntled .

At one point, the chair umpire had to pause the match , saying, "Guys, please, in the suite behind me … please take your seat." It's unclear whether it was directed at the same group.

Commenters in those social media posts weren't pleased to see content creators disrespecting the game. "Between influencers, corporate wining and dining, and bots, ticket prices are sky high and yet empty seats abound," one wrote.

"This is extremely sad and disappointing because there are soooo many true tennis fans that would kill to have this experience to go to the US open & tix are getting so [expensive]," another said.

After the match, Osaka said that while influencers can help "make the sport of tennis popular," the distractions "have to be managed a lot better."

"If you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," she added.

American tennis stars Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff also chimed in on the controversy, with Pegula saying that influencer behavior has " gotten a little maybe too much " this year and Gauff noting that camera flashes can be distracting.

That group of influencers wasn't the only one drawing attention away from tennis, either. Another video shows a group of men showing off their outfits, appearing to prioritize caviar chicken nuggets and fashion over the sport. And let's not forget how many people have complained that the stadium is just loud in general now , abandoning the quiet spectatorship traditionally associated with tennis. As one TikToker suggested , some creators seem more focused on getting content than enjoying the experience.

Bad etiquette should be an easy fix. The brands that bring influencers along could just fill them in on the nuances of tennis culture. "If you're being invited to [a] red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans," Gauff said. It would also help prevent bad publicity for the brands, which are likely being tagged in posts by the influencers they invited to their suites.

I can't help but notice that, even if influencers behaved with perfect politeness at the U.S. Open, some people would still openly resent them. I saw the same comment echoed on multiple posts : "Influencers ruin everything."

They're marketers, so content creation is their job. But psychologist Sal Raichbach told Yahoo that audiences "disconnect" when they're obviously being sold something. On top of that, the access given to influencers is not something many fans can afford these days .

"Humans typically react very differently to things we believe were offered freely, versus things we assume were designed to influence us or demonstrate status," he said.

It doesn't help that influencers tend to post the same content at the U.S. Open — outfit photos in front of the courts, and tours of spaces that most people may never be able to access. They're all grabbing a Honey Deuce , the event's signature drink, or a $38 French Dip sandwich from Salt Hank's .

Jennifer Neeley, a strategic marketing adviser and instructor in digital marketing and influencer marketing at UC San Diego, told Yahoo that influencer fatigue really kicks in "when creator access starts to feel more visible than the event itself."

It shines a spotlight on just how many of them are not actually there for tennis, she said.

The problem, Neeley explained, is not the influencers; it's the "promotional sameness." The same pageantry and tradition that make the tennis tournament charming is the downfall of the influencers who promote it, and the solution might be to offer a new point of view instead of repeating the same old content.

And maybe studying up on tennis before attending one of the sport's biggest events will help too.

articles.title: xQc slams modern subathons as ‘begging for money’, says streamers now use them to maximize income
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Felix “xQc” Lengyel has explained why he has never hosted a subathon, and his view on the streaming trend is far from positive. During a recent stream.
articles.body: Felix “xQc” Lengyel has explained why he has never hosted a subathon, and his view on the streaming trend is far from positive. During a recent stream with his father, the popular Twitch and Kick streamer was asked whether he had ever done a subathon. xQc used the question to explain how the format was originally used by streamers and why he believes its purpose has changed. While he acknowledged that subathons once helped creators earn enough money to get through several weeks or months, he argued that many streamers now use them simply to maximize their income.xQc says subathons have changed from survival to maximizing incomeThe discussion came during xQc’s September 3 stream, where he and his father answered some of the most searched questions about the streamer. The questions covered everything from his net worth and music preferences to his history with subathons.When asked whether he had ever done one, xQc called the question a strange one before explaining how the format was viewed in the earlier days of streaming.He said:“Way back in the day, like ages ago, people wouldn’t have to beg for money, right? Or whatever, because there were fewer subs back then, right? Fewer subscribers overall, and no Twitch subscribers. So people didn’t like begging for money because it’s lame, let’s be honest. Begging for money is lame.”According to xQc, streamers would sometimes run a subathon for two or three days. The goal was not necessarily to keep the event going for as long as possible. Instead, creators could use the money earned during that period to cover their expenses for the rest of the month or even longer.“So they would do one subathon, right? And it would last for, like, two or three days, right? And then they would have a good amount of money for the rest of the month, right? Even for months on end. So they were, like, good on money,” he continued.However, xQc believes the format has evolved.“But these days, nobody does that for that. Nowadays, subathons are, like, just a way to get, like, the most money possible,” he said.The streamer argued that modern subathons are less about simply supporting a creator through a difficult period and more about building up their earnings. He compared the approach to repeatedly asking viewers for financial support, even when the streamer is already financially secure.“Another way to survive is just a way to, like, build some stacks. But it’s, like, this guy’s, in a way, like, ‘Guys, support me,’ whatever, but their support… I mean, they have it in the bank, you know?” xQc added.His comments also explain why he has never felt the need to use the format himself.xQc recalls meeting Donald Trump in 2024The same stream produced another interesting moment when xQc was asked whether he had ever met Donald Trump.The streamer and his father confirmed that he had met the former US president in August 2024. xQc then recalled that Trump was polite during their interaction and spent more time with him than he expected.“He was very polite, and he was very welcoming, too. Yeah, and he spent more time than he had to. And I knew he was busy,” xQc said.The comments came while xQc was answering several personal questions alongside his father, giving viewers a glimpse into some of his experiences away from his regular streaming content.His remarks about subathons, however, were the more pointed part of the discussion. xQc did not reject the idea of viewers supporting streamers. Instead, his criticism was aimed at how he believes the format is now being used by some creators.For xQc, the difference comes down to purpose. He sees the older version of the subathon as a short-term way for streamers to secure enough income to keep going. Modern versions, in his view, are more focused on pushing subscription numbers and maximizing earnings.xQc explained why he has never hosted a subathon, arguing that the format has changed from a short-term way for streamers to secure enough money to survive into a tool for maximizing earnings. He also recalled meeting Donald Trump in August 2024, describing the former president as polite, welcoming, and willing to spend more time with him than expected.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bay Area hiker rescued after reporting mountain lion stalking him near San Jose
articles.summary: A hiker was rescued by a Santa Clara County sheriff's helicopter after he reported that a mountain lion was stalking him on the Boccardo Loop Trail near San...
articles.body:
A Bay Area hiker was airlifted to safety after reporting that he was stalked by a mountain lion on a trail in the foothills east of San Jose.

The hiker was walking the Boccardo Loop Trail inside Sierra Vista Open Space Preserve late last week when he said that a mountain lion was following him, according to the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office.

With limited cellphone service and concerned that he could not safely continue, the man stopped about two miles from the trailhead and called for help, the sheriff's office said.

The department's helicopter responded to assist San Jose police, located the hiker and landed to pick him up. He was brought out of the preserve without injury.

Sierra Vista Open Space Preserve is home to mountain lions, along with bobcats and other wildlife, according to the Santa Clara Valley Open Space Authority. The 1,611-acre preserve has about nine miles of trails and sits in the eastern foothills of Santa Clara County.

Mountain lions generally avoid people, and attacks are rare, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife says.

People who encounter one are advised not to run or turn their backs on the animal. Instead, CDFW recommends facing the mountain lion, remaining calm, making noise, making yourself appear larger and giving the animal a way to escape.

The agency's published records list fewer than 50 verified mountain lion attacks on humans in California since 1890, including six that were fatal.

Its most recent published list, updated in August 2025, includes several nonfatal attacks in Santa Clara County, including one involving a child in Cupertino in 2014 and another in Rancho San Antonio County Park in 2020.

The Open Space Authority advises visitors to stay alert in mountain lion habitat and not hike, bike or jog alone. If a mountain lion is encountered, visitors should keep their distance, avoid approaching the animal and leave the area once it is safe to do so.
